result.summary: This is the surface of the translate-c Zig package: its build.zig, the Translator build helper and the test-case lowering code. Together they build the translate-c executable on top of the pinned aro dependency and wire Run steps that translate C headers into Zig modules. I checked the build-time code for network access, execution of anything other than the package's own artifact, reads outside the package and build cache, and encoded payloads, and found none; no file is marked as missing from the source repository.

findings.title: advapi32 linked on Windows
findings.detail: On Windows targets the translate-c tool links advapi32. This is consistent with Windows SDK and MSVC detection through the registry in the aro and Zig toolchain code; Zig's own translate-c does the same. Nothing in the surface uses it for anything else.

findings.title: Pinned aro dependency
findings.detail: The aro dependency is fetched from codeberg.org/ziglang/arocc at a fixed commit and pinned by a content hash, so its contents cannot change silently.

findings.title: Test case discovery at build configuration time
findings.detail: lowerCases opens test/cases while the build graph is configured. That directory is not in the package's .paths, so for consumers the open fails and only a fail step is attached to the test steps. The code only parses test manifests and builds test steps; nothing runs unless the test steps are invoked.

data_flows.what: The C source path, include and framework paths, macro definitions, target triple and translation flags go to the translate-c executable as arguments. It writes the generated .zig file and a deps.d dependency file as build outputs.
data_flows.to: translate-c child process run by the Zig build system, writing into the build cache

data_flows.what: Installs the translate-c executable, aro's builtin include directory and the package's lib/ directory into the build's install prefix. Standard Zig build install steps.
